column4: The section pictures ilham as something Allah places within the self; this verse says Allah will cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers. The inward placement recurs with an opposite content and audience, distinguishing moral orientation from fear imposed in battle.

The section joins divine inward instruction to maternal nourishment; 20:38 says Allah inspired Moses’ mother. The next verse, 20:39, supplies the content of that inspiration, while this ayah’s own contribution is to identify the mother as its recipient.

The section describes ilham as something cast into the inner person; 20:39 tells Moses’ mother to place him in a chest and the river, then says Allah cast love upon him. This gives the casting image a concrete infant scene; 20:38 identifies the command as inspiration to his mother.

The source section uses ن ف س for the self and says it receives both fujur and taqwa; 12:53 describes the nafs as urging evil, with an exception for those shown mercy by their Lord. It specifies the evilward tendency while bounding it by divine mercy.

The section’s root س ق ي describes giving someone drink, and its dictionary note on ر س ل evokes successive milk; 23:21 says God gives people drink from livestock’s bellies. Alongside the camel’s assigned water share, this adds the complementary scene of an animal supplying drink to people.
